# A test reads a node's one-way prop, `c.g.quiet[1][0].value`, which is the
# expression its call site gave read through the instance: here the element of
# a loop walking what a method of the component answers. The method was called
# as the component's own body calls it, with no instance, which no compiled
# test can name (`/* unresolved method grid.plain */`); it is called through
# the instance now, a method reading a context included.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '^ok +2 tests, 0 failures$'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

context #suffix("!")

func shout(s string) => s + suffix

// Each loop walks what a method of the component answers.
component grid ui.node {
    var cells = [["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]]

    func plain() => cells

    func loud() => cells.map(func(r list[string]) => r.map(func(s string) => shout(s)))

    ui.vbox {
        for var row = plain() {
            for var cell = row {
                ui.text #quiet(value=cell)
            }
        }
        for var row = loud() {
            for var cell = row {
                ui.text #noisy(value=cell)
            }
        }
    }
}

component host ui.node {
    grid #g()
}

func testReadsThroughAMethod(t test.Test, c host) {
    t.assert(c.g.quiet[1][0].value == "c")
}

func testReadsThroughAMethodReadingAContext(t test.Test, c host) {
    t.assert(c.g.noisy[1][0].value == "c!")
}
